newsitem.title: CHINA: N.Korea says U.S. planes spied 2,000 times in 1996.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea says U.S. planes spied 2,000 times in 1996.

text.p: The United States sent planes on more than 2,000 sorties to spy on North Korea in 1996, the Xinhua news agency quoted newspapers in Pyongyang as saying on Sunday.

The United States sent surveillance planes over North Korea an average of 120 times per month in 1996 from its military bases in Japan and South Korea, the newspapers said, quoting documents from the North Korean military.
Xinhua did not explain the discrepancy in the figures.

On Thursday and Friday of last week, three U.S. surveillance planes flew over the military demarcation line between North and South Korea and spied on strategic targets in the North, Xinhua quoted the newspapers as saying. It gave no more details.
The newspaper reports came as the United States was expecting an apology from North Korea over the incursion of a submarine carrying 26 heavily-armed agents into South Korea in September.

The United States said its diplomats seeking an apology from North Korea over the submarine incident held "serious and useful" talks with Pyongyang envoys, and media reports on Sunday said an apology was imminent.

South Korean and Japanese media said North Korea may apologise as early as Sunday for what South Korean President Kim Young-sam condemned as a "military provocation" that violated a truce that ended the 1950-53 Korean War. He froze all contacts with the North and warned of "all-out war".

Last October, the United States said it had sent an advanced reconnaissance plane to monitor the possible test firing by North Korea of a medium-range ballistic missile into seas just off the Japanese coast.
